svg.text: migrate-workload — eight phases, eight gates, one rollback path
Moves a workload off EC2, ECS, Docker Compose, or a VM onto EKS managed by Argo CD. The source stays live until Phase 7.
.kiro/skills/migrate-workload/SKILL.md · the largest skill, and the only one with progressive disclosure via references/
Three rules that hold across every phase
fires on "migrate", "move", "port", "containerise", "modernise", or "moving off EC2/ECS/Compose"
This is the only skill built as a gated pipeline rather than a scaffold — the ordering carries the safety, not the output.
1 — A gate ends every phase
Do not start a phase until the previous gate has passed.
If a gate fails, fix the cause and re-run that phase — never skip ahead.
2 — The source stays live until Phase 7
Every phase before cutover is purely additive, so there is
a rollback path available at all times.
3 — references/ load lazily
Read a reference file only when the phase needing it begins.
They are detail, not context you need up front.
Discover — build an inventory of the source workload
read live configuration with the AWS MCP tools; ask only for what you cannot observe
Capture all thirteen. This is the phase everything downstream is translated from, so a gap here becomes a wrong manifest later.
runtime and version
entrypoint
listening ports
environment variables
secrets, and where they come from
mounted volumes, and whether they hold state
CPU and memory actually in use
health check endpoint
outbound dependencies
inbound traffic path
IAM permissions in use
log destination
current scaling behaviour
references/discovery-checklist.md has the per-source-type commands.
GATE · the inventory is complete and every environment variable and IAM permission is accounted for. Any unresolved "unknown" is a blocker, not a footnote.
Containerise
skip entirely if a suitable image already exists

text.tspan: Write a Dockerfile with all six properties:

svg.text: multi-stage build
minimal runtime base image
non-root user
no secrets in layers
EXPOSE
stated explicitly
HEALTHCHECK
where the runtime supports one
Build for linux/amd64 unless the cluster runs arm64 nodes.
Then run it locally with the same environment variables as production — that is what makes the gate meaningful.
GATE · the container starts and its health endpoint responds successfully.
Publish the image
into the existing project ECR repository named after the app
Do not create the repository — it is managed elsewhere. Retag and push:
111122223333.dkr.ecr.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/<app>:<tag>
If the source already lives on Docker Hub, GHCR, or elsewhere, retag and push into that ECR repository — do not leave the upstream registry in the manifests.
GATE · the image is resolvable by digest from 111122223333.dkr.ecr.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/<app>
Cluster readiness
confirm the target cluster already has what this workload needs
Which components are required depends on the workload, so this list is conditional rather than fixed:
an ingress controller — if the app serves traffic
a CSI driver — if it needs volumes
an autoscaler — if it is a queue-worker
the secrets backend named in the project profile
On EKS Auto Mode the load balancer controller, storage driver, and node lifecycle are managed for you — do not install them.
GATE · every required controller or CRD is present.
Missing platform components are a change to the platform repo — not something to bundle into the app.
Identity and secrets
the phase where copying the old setup is the tempting mistake
Write apps/<app>/iam.tf from the permissions inventoried in Phase 0 — not from a copy of the source instance profile.
IAM — one role per workload
Declares the IAM policy and the Pod Identity association.
Shape comes from the identity-and-secrets steering file, or
references/iam-templates.md if the app needs IRSA instead.
Secrets — a SecretProviderClass in both overlays
region: ap-southeast-2 · usePodIdentity: "true" · secretObjects
Wire the CSI volume, mount, and secretKeyRef in the patch.
Add secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on those ARNs to iam.tf.
Apply Terraform for dev-eks-1 now; prod follows at promotion. Secrets Manager values are created out of band — this workflow only references them.
GATE · the association exists and resolves to the intended ServiceAccount, and every secret path referenced by the manifests exists in Secrets Manager.
Both overlays have a matching SecretProviderClass when secrets are required.
Generate GitOps manifests
this phase is the add-app skill, with the inventory already in hand
Choose the archetype, then scaffold base and both overlays. Follow add-app for file-by-file detail.
Translate the inventory rather than transcribing it — each source concept has a Kubernetes counterpart that is not a literal copy:
Source (what you inventoried in Phase 0)
Kubernetes (what you write in Phase 5)
Instance count
replicas, or autoscaler bounds
Instance type sizing
Resource requests and limits, from observed usage
Instance profile
Per-workload IAM role
Security group rules
Load balancer listener
Service plus Ingress
.env file or Parameter Store lookups at boot
Overlay SecretProviderClass + secretKeyRef
Host log agent
Container stdout plus a cluster log forwarder
Cron entry on the host
references/manifest-patterns.md has the manifest skeletons.
GATE · kustomize build succeeds for base and both overlays, and policy validation passes.
Sync and verify on dev
the first phase where a human gate exists — nothing reaches the cluster without a merge
Commit on a branch
Open a PR · let CI run
Human merges
ApplicationSet picks up the overlay
Argo CD syncs to dev-eks-1
Application reports Synced and Healthy
all pods Running and Ready
logs show no startup errors
reaches AWS dependencies via its new role
health endpoint responds through the new load balancer
GATE · Argo CD reports Healthy on dev-eks-1 and the health endpoint responds.
Promote and cut over
use the promote-app skill for the digest copy — summarised here
Apply iam.tf for prod-eks-1 if the association is not already there.
Copy the verified image digest from the dev overlay pin to the prod overlay pin. Do not rebuild.
Merge, then confirm <app>-prod-eks-1 is Synced and Healthy.
Then shift traffic at DNS. Use weighted routing for a gradual shift when the app is user-facing, and watch error rates and latency across the shift.
GATE · all traffic is on the new endpoint and error rates match the pre-migration baseline.
R
Rollback — a named path, kept available until Phase 8
this is why the source workload and its load balancer stay up through Phase 7
Each failure mode has one prescribed action. None of them involve deleting anything on EKS:
Problem
Action
Prod Argo app unhealthy after digest promote
Revert the promote PR, or restore the previous prod digest. Leave digests alone otherwise.
Errors spike after the DNS weight shift
Move DNS weight back to the old endpoint. Leave the EKS app running.
Need a hard abort
Point DNS fully at the old stack. Do not delete EKS resources yet.
Do not start Phase 8 until cutover has been stable for a full business cycle. Rollback after decommission is a rebuild, not a flip.
Decommission
only after the cutover has been stable long enough to trust — a full business cycle at minimum
Remove the old compute, its load balancer and target groups, its instance profile, and any deployment artefacts.
Record what was deleted. A migration with no record of what was removed is a migration nobody can audit afterwards.
GATE · explicit human confirmation. Never delete source infrastructure automatically.
Post-migration — three things that reliably break later if skipped
the migration is not finished at cutover
Observability
Host dashboards keyed on instance IDs are now
meaningless. Rebuild around pod, deployment, and
namespace dimensions; forward stdout to your backend.
Alerting
Add alerts for pod restart counts, rollout failures,
and error rate at the ingress. The old instance-health
alarms no longer fire on anything real.
Runbooks
Instance-based procedures do not translate — there is
no SSH to a node on EKS Auto Mode. Rewrite around
kubectl logs/describe/rollout restart + debug containers.
Scope — this workflow assumes a stateless workload
Stateful workloads need persistent volume claims, a StatefulSet, and a data migration plan with its own cutover. Treat that as a separate exercise — do not fold it into these phases.
discover → containerise → publish → cluster ready → identity → manifests → verify on dev → promote and cut over → decommission (human confirms)
